newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-ROBSON LOOKS SET TO LEAVE BARCELONA A WINNER.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ROBSON LOOKS SET TO LEAVE BARCELONA A WINNER.

text.p: If English coach Bobby Robson leaves Barcelona this week -- as has been widely anticipated over the last few days -- at least he will go out a winner.
Barcelona beat Racing Santander 1-0 on Sunday to narrow the gap on the Spanish league leaders Real Madrid to six points, following Madrid's 2-2 draw with Real Betis on Saturday.

Spanish media have strongly predicted that Robson will leave Barcelona on Monday or Tuesday after less than a season at the Nou Camp, despite Barcelona beating Real Madrid recently in the Spanish Cup.
Other action from around Europe included:
ENGLAND

The shock results continued in the F.A. Cup with second division Chesterfield scoring a memorable 1-0 win over premier league Nottingham Forest to reach the quarter-finals for the first time since they were formed in 1866. They will meet second division rivals Wrexham in the last eight, following the Welsh team's shock 3-1 win at Birmingham. First division Portsmouth stunned premier league Leeds 3-2. There were wins for Middlesbrough, Wimbledon and Sheffield Wednesday.
There were only two premier league matches with Tottenham drawing 0-0 with Arsenal in the 124th North London derby and Derby beating West Ham 1-0.
NETHERLANDS

PSV's poor start to the second half of the Dutch season continued on Sunday when they lost 1-0 at Vitesse to allow Feyenoord, 2-0 winners at Volendam, to go level on points at the top of the standings.
Both sides have 48 points from 21 games, with PSV holding on to top spot on goal difference.
Twente Enschede beat Roda 3-1 on Saturday to stay third on 43 points.
ITALY

Juventus pulled five points clear of the field at the top of Serie A on Sunday when they won 2-1 at home against struggling Perugia and second placed Sampdoria went down the same score at home to Roma for their first defeat in eight games. Alessandro del Piero scored both of Juve's goals, the first from the penalty spot after 37 minutes and the second with a turn and shot eight minutes later.
Bologna's hopes of their first title since 1964 were dealt a heavy blow when they lost 2-0 at Milan.
GERMANY
Juergen Klinsmann marked the re-start of the German season after the winter break with two goals in Bayern Munich's 3-0 home win over St Pauli on Saturday which put his side back on top of the table.
Reigning champions Borussia Dortmund briefly went top on Friday night when they also returned to action in good form, beating third-placed Bayer Leverkusen 3-1 with Andy Moeller scoring twice.
FRANCE
Sonny Anderson of Brazil scored twice as French league leaders Monaco beat Le Havre 3-0 on Friday to move seven points clear of Paris St Germain at the top of the table.

PSG had cut Monaco's lead to four points after a 2-1 win over Lens on Thursday. But that match was marred when a linesman was knocked out after being hit by a missile thrown from the crowd. Lens are likely to receive a tough punishment from the French league for the incident.
